correctness.rationale: For a simple connected graph, individual weights inject into the grounded Laplacian, making logdet strictly concave and the maximizing allocation unique. The exact two-terminal spanning-tree polynomial is invariant under independent within-path edge permutations, forcing the pathwise equalization at the global optimum. For normalized path budgets, the objective is sum_i(ell_i-1)log x_i+log(x_0+sum_i x_i/ell_i²). Its homogeneous KKT multiplier is rho. The direct-edge stationarity yields a*=B(1-S)/rho for S<=1; the boundary equations have a unique strictly decreasing scalar root xi, with boundary complementarity exactly xi>=1 iff S>=1. All path allocations are positive and correctly sum to B. Exact rational determinants and full unsymmetrized numerical maximizations verify representative cases; infinite validity is analytic.

value.rationale: A fixed per-edge conductance budget raises a natural network-design decision: fund or omit an already available direct terminal link, despite the objective strictly increasing in its weight when every other edge is held fixed. The sharp criterion sum_i 1/(ell_i+1)>=1, the unique optimum for arbitrarily many heterogeneous paths, and the root-defined post-threshold allocation expose a genuine support phase boundary and offer an exact reusable design rule. It is neither merely a numeric example nor a routine restatement of general logdet concavity.
